initialReview.template: Use a freshly fingerprinted SoftwareX Original Software Publication Word or LaTeX template and do not deviate widely from its prescribed structure; preserve the five mandatory main sections. Current fingerprints: DOCX 9fcf40ed...916d and TeX 2b18dfd1...8649. Word figures must be embedded in the DOCX.
initialReview.layout: Preserve the five mandatory main sections: Motivation and significance; Software description with architecture and functionality; at least one Illustrative example; Impact; Conclusions. Main text is normally no more than six pages excluding metadata, tables, figures and references, with the 4,000-word limit taking priority.
initialReview.anonymity: The current Guide states single-anonymized review. Author names and affiliations are visible to reviewers and must be supplied accurately; no double-anonymous stripping is authorized.
initialReview.acceptedFiles: The current Guide states the expected roles: Word uses the DOCX in Manuscript (Word or PDF file); LaTeX uses a rendered PDF there plus a ZIP of complete TeX, figure and bibliography sources in Zip file containing LaTeX source files. These are Guide-derived expectations, not a verified live SelCal portal slot map. Treat the current portal configuration as UNVERIFIED until a fresh SoftwareX draft is inspected.
initialReview.lengthAndCounting: Maximum 4,000 words, excluding title, authors, affiliations, references and metadata tables, but including abstract, running text, captions and footnotes. Maximum six figures. Apply the stricter joint bounds of an approximately 100-word abstract that is also at most 250 words, and one to six keywords.
initialReview.frontMatter: Use a short software-name title, confirmed authors and developer affiliations, an approximately 100-word factual abstract, one to six English keywords and complete metadata entries C1-C8. Highlights and a graphical abstract are encouraged rather than treated as current hard requirements.
initialReview.figuresAndTables: Use no more than six figures. Include a compact architecture overview and evidence-bearing evaluation graphics. Because the journal-specific Word instruction requires embedded figures while the generic figure section requests separate files, retain embedded figures plus separate source-quality figure files until the live portal map resolves the upload roles.
initialReview.accessibility: Provide readable labels, self-contained captions, defined symbols, color-safe encodings and alt text where requested. Render and inspect the exact manuscript bytes before upload.
initialReview.references: Cite methods, comparators, datasets and software with versions. The current Guide recommends a software PID or DOI where available, but it is not recorded here as a submission hard gate and does not replace metadata C2. Verified full-text exemplars may guide structure and evidence order only, never wording, numbers, results or unearned claims.
initialReview.endMatter: Include only confirmed acknowledgements, CRediT roles, funding and sponsor role, competing-interest declaration, data availability, applicable ethics and rights statements, and a generative-AI manuscript-preparation declaration when such tools were used beyond exempt basic checks.
initialReview.supplementaryMaterials: Submit relevant supplementary material or supplementary data together with the manuscript. The repository or supplements must expose validation matrices, exact-oracle fixtures, adverse results, comparator logs, clean-install receipts, provenance, environment and dependency identities without hiding decision-changing failures.
initialReview.fileNamingAndMetadata: Official current Guide layer: public GitHub, README.md, LICENSE.txt and source in repository-root src. Current template layer: GitHub, README.md, Licence.txt and metadata C1-C8 including C1 current version, C2 permanent GitHub link and C3 legal code licence. Internal reproducibility layer, not a journal-explicit hard rule: freeze an exact release or tag and prefer a PID when available. After the author selects the code licence, retain auditable same-content LICENSE.txt and Licence.txt compatibility files. Build the final slot map only from a fresh SelCal portal draft.

requirements.requirement: SelCal must be publicly inspectable, validatable and reusable research software with evidenced potential or demonstrated impact on scientific discovery; engineering completeness alone is insufficient.
Use the current OSP template with five mandatory body sections, an approximately 100-word abstract, one to six keywords, a 4,000-word limit and no more than six figures.

The public GitHub distribution must contain README.md, the required code-licence identification and source in repository-root src; metadata C1-C8 must be complete and bind the submitted software version. Release or tag freezing is an internal reproducibility control unless a current official source makes it explicit.
Provide empirical evidence that SelCal enables new research questions or improves pursuit of existing questions and has a credible reuse path; usefulness assertions do not satisfy the Impact section.
The experimental setting, empirical evaluation, comparison with prior work and results must be clear, reproducible and proportionate to the claimed impact.

Independent reviewers must be able to install, build or deploy SelCal, run documented examples, reproduce compatible results, inspect automated tests and API or user documentation, and verify environment, dependency, portability, maintainability and licence statements.
Deposit relevant validation data in a suitable repository and cite and link it, or provide a truthful reason it cannot be shared; submit a data availability statement.
Code quality, testing, maintenance and licensing claims must bind the exact submitted source. P3-derived materials and third-party dependencies require explicit source and distribution boundaries.
Before submission, inspect a new SelCal portal draft and bind the live article type, author fields, declarations, file roles, metadata, converted review PDF and final receipts.
